abstract.value: The DataCite Ontology is an ontology written in OWL 2 DL to enable the metadata properties of the [DataCite Metadata Schema (version 4.7)](https://datacite-metadata-schema.readthedocs.io/en/4.7/) to be described in RDF.

scopeNote.value: An organization identifier belongs to a particular identifier scheme, such as ISNI, specified by an individual within the class datacite:OrganizationIdentifierScheme.

comment.en: An identifier that uniquely identities an individual organization.

scopeNote.value: A personal identifier belongs to a particular identifier scheme, such as ORCID, specified by an individual within the class datacite:PersonalIdentifierScheme.

comment.en: An identifier that uniquely identifies an individual person.

scopeNote.value: An identifier belongs to a particular scheme, such as those specified by individuals of the class datacite:IdentifierScheme.

comment.en: An identifier that uniquely identities an entity, such as a funding agency, a person or a resource.

scopeNote.value: Individual schemes are defines as members of this class. For DataCite, the only permitted identifier scheme for the primary resource identifier is the Digital Object Identifier (datacite:doi).

comment.en: The Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a unique identifier for abstract or physical resources.
The Life Science Identifier (LSID) is a unique identifier used for uniquely naming significant resources in the biology domain.

scopeNote.value: An RRID name is divided into two parts, the authority and a local identifier, separated by an underscore.

comment.en: The Research Resource IDentifier (RRID) is a character string used to uniquely identify key inputs to an experiment including the so-called “key biological resources” as defined by the National Institutes of Health, and related tools such as core facilities and databases.
The Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is a unique identifier for a resource retrievable on the World Wide Web.

scopeNote.value: A DBLP publication identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://dblp.org/rec/<identifier>.

comment.en: The DBLP publication identifier is a unique key that identifies a specific publication record, conference, or journal registered on DBLP.
The Uniform Resource Name (URN) is a unique identifier for a resource, following the URN scheme.

scopeNote.value: A DOI is resolvable from the following URL: http://www.doi.org/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Digital Object Identier (DOI) is a unique identifier assigned to identify digital objects.

scopeNote.value: An OCLC control number is resolvable from the following URL: https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/<identifier>.

comment.en: The OCLC control number is a unique identifier assigned by OCLC to each bibliographic record input into WorldCat.
The PubMed Identifier (PMID) is a bibliographic identifier for the PubMed database.
A resource identifier scheme that provides local resource identifiers that are unique in their local environment and understood by the person submitting the metadata.
The International Standard Text Code (ISTC) is a standard designed to uniquely identify textual works.
The Bibliographic Code (BIBCODE) is a 19 ASCII characters identifier which describes a journal article.

scopeNote.value: A Wikipedia page name is resolvable from the following URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Wikipedia page name is a unique identifier used to refer to any entity present in a Wikipedia database.
The Persistent Uniform Resource Locator (PURL) is a URL that is used to redirect to the location of a requested web resource.
The Serial Item and Contribution Identifier (SICI) is a code used to uniquely identify specific volumes, articles or other identifiable parts of a serial.
The Publisher Item Identifier is a unique identifier used by several scientific journal publishers to identify documents.

scopeNote.value: An ArXiv ID is resolvable using the following URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/<identifier>.

comment.en: The ArXiv ID is a unique identifier for ArXiv (http://arxiv.org/), a open access repository of preprints.
The Linking International Standard Serial Number (LISSN) is an identifier that connects different media versions of the same serial publication.
The NIH Manuscript Submission Identifier (NIHMSID) is a preliminary article identifier that applies only to manuscripts deposited through the NIHMS system.
The Info URI scheme is a standardized method for identifying information assets that have public identifiers (like ISBNs, DOIs, or LCCNs) but lack a native URI representation.
The PubMed Central Identifier (PMCID) is a bibliographic identifier for the PubMed Central database.
The Open Citation Identifier (OCI) is a persistent identifier for bibliographic citations, created and maintained by OpenCitations (http://opencitations.net).
The International Standard Serial Number (ISSN) is an eight-digit code to uniquely identify a periodical publication, such as a magazine.

scopeNote.value: A DNB catalogue number is resolvable from the following URL: https://d-nb.info/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Deutsche Nationalbibliothek (DNB) catalogue number is a unique identifier assigned to every entry in the DNB catalogue.

scopeNote.value: A Common Science and Technology Resources Identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://www.cstr.cn/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Common Science and Technology Resources (CSTR) Identifier is an identifier based on the Chinese National Standard GB/T 32843—2016 “Science and technology resource identification”, providing a unique identification service for scientific data, papers, scientific institutions, researchers, scientific instruments, patents and other scientific and technological resources.
An Archival Resource Key (ARK) is a multi-purpose URL suited to being a persistent identifier for information objects of any type.

scopeNote.value: A SPDX identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://spdx.org/licenses/<identifier>.

comment.en: The SPDX License List is a list of commonly found licenses and exceptions used in free and open source and other collaborative software or documentation.
The International Article Number is a unique 13-digit barcode standard used worldwide to identify retail products.
The International Standard Book Number (ISBN) is a unique 13-digit commercial identifier for books and monographic publications.
The Universal Product Code (UPC) is a unique number used to identify products and their manufacturers.
The Electronic International Standard Serial Number (eISSN) is an eight-digit identifier specifically for electronic versions of serials, such as online journals, databases, or websites.
The International Generic Sample Number (IGSN) is a code that uniquely identifies samples from our natural environment and related features-of-interest.
The Handle System is a distributed computing technology that provides unique, persistent identifiers (handles) for digital resources, allowing them to be located over time regardless of URL changes.
The identifier scheme used to identify a resource.

comment.undefined:
Any region in a dimensional space (a dimensional space is a maximal Region), which can be used as a value for a quality of an Entity . For example, TimeInterval, SpaceRegion, PhysicalAttribute, Amount, SocialAttribute are all subclasses of Region. 
Regions are not data values in the ordinary knowledge representation sense; in order to get patterns for modelling data, see the properties: representsDataValue and hasDataValue

scopeNote.value: Individual schemes are defines as members of this class. At present, the only individual of this class is datacite:fundref.

comment.en: A funder identifier scheme that provides local funder identifiers that are unique in their local environment and understood by the person submitting the metadata.

The FundRef identifier is a unique code assigned by Fundref, a collaborative pilot project of scholarly publishers and funding agencies, facilitated by CrossRef, to provide a standard way of identifying and reporting funding sources for published scholarly research.
The identifier scheme used to identify a funding agency.
A description in a research paper documenting the specialized methods used in the work described.
Used to charactierize a description of a resource that is part of a series.
A catch-all description type required by the DataCite Metadata Schema to characterize description types that are not abstracts, series information or tables of content.

A table of content giving information about the content of a resource, appearing before the body text. Where the resource is a journal or magazine issue, the table of content lists the constituent items contained in that issue, typically by title, authors and first page number.
A brief summary of a textual work, appearing at the beginning of the work and designed to act as the point-of-entry that will help the reader quickly to obtain an overview of the work's contents.
This class permits classification of the type of description given to a resource described by the DataCite Metadata schema.

scopeNote.value: Individual schemes are defines as members of this class.
A Gemeinsame Normdatei identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://d-nb.info/gnd/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND) identifier is a unique key assigned to authority data managed by the German National Library.

scopeNote.value: Such identifiers are RFC 3986-compliant URIs with a scheme of spase, and only implementing the authority and path parts of the specification. Thus, their generic form is: spase://<authority><path>.

comment.undefined: The SPASE resource identifier is the identifier of resources included in the resource registry (datasets, instruments, observatories, etc) maintained by the Space Physics Archive Search and Extract (SPASE) group.

scopeNote.value: A Library of Congress authority identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://id.loc.gov/authorities/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Library of Congress (LoC) authority identifier is a unique identifier used for authority control in the Library of Congress.
The SciGraph ID is an unique identifier used for referring to entities in the Springer Nature SciGraph dataset.

scopeNote.value: A Wikidata QID is resolvable from the following URL: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Wikidata QID is a unique identifier used for the entities in Wikidata.

scopeNote.value: It has the shape of a URL starting with "https://w3id.org/" plus a local identifier that completes it (e.g. "https://w3id.org/changes").

comment.undefined: The W3id.org identifier is a secure, permanent URL re-direction service for Web applications, run by the W3C Permanent Identifier Community Group.

scopeNote.value: An OpenAlex ID has two parts. The first part is the base, that is always https://openalex.org/. The second part is the key, i.e. the unique primary key that identifies a given resource in our database. The key starts with a letter that tells us the kind of entity: W(ork), A(uthor), V(enue), I(nstitution), or C(oncept). In addition, the IDs are not case-sensitive, so w2741809807 is just as valid as W2741809807.

comment.en: The OpenAlex ID is a unique identifier assigned to each entity included in OpenAlex.

scopeNote.value: These identifiers are RFC 3986-compliant URIs with a scheme of ivo. Thus, their generic form is: ivo://<authority><path>?<query>#<fragment>.

comment.en: The IVOA identifier (IVOID) is the identifier of resources within the resource registry (datasets, data access services, etc.) maintained by the International Virtual Observatory Alliance (IVOA).

scopeNote.value: The OMID is structured as follows: [[entity_type_abbreviation]]/[[supplier_prefix]][[sequential_number]] (e.g. "br/0601", where "br" is the entity type, "060" is the supplier prefix, and "1" is the sequential number).

comment.en: The OpenCitations Meta Identifier (OMID) is a persistent identifier for bibliographic resources, created and maintained by OpenCitations (http://opencitations.net).
The identifier scheme used to identify an entity such as a funding agency, a person or a resource.

scopeNote.value: Individual schemes are defines as members of this class.
A IEEE Xplore author ID is resolvable from the following URL: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/<identifier>.

comment.en: The IEEE Xplore author ID is a unique identifier assigned to authors in IEEE Xplore.

scopeNote.value: The ACM Digital Library author ID is resolvable using the following URL: https://dl.acm.org/profile/<identifier>.

comment.en: An ACM Digital Library author ID is a unique identifier found within an ACM Author Profile Page, which consolidates an researcher's publications, citations, and metadata.
The Japanese Science and Technology Agency (JST) identifier is a unique code assigned to scientific research products by the Japan Science and Technology Agency.

scopeNote.value: A zbMATH author identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=ai:<identifier>.

comment.en: The zbMATH author identifier is a unique identifier used for a person in the Zentralblatt MATH database.
The United Kingdom National Insurance Number is a code used to uniquely identify in the tax system, banking, social welfare, online government services and electoral registration.
The National Individual Identifier (NII) is a unique number assigned to citizens, residents and visitors for tracking and verification purposes.

scopeNote.value: A Mathematics Genealogy Project identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=<identifier>.

comment.en: The Mathematics Genealogy Project identifier is an identifier for mathematicians and computer scientists at the Mathematics Genealogy Project.

scopeNote.value: A RePEc Short Identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://authors.repec.org/pro/<identifier>.

comment.en: The RePEc Short identifier is a unique, permanent identifier for researchers registered in the RePEc Author Service.

scopeNote.value: An ISNI is resolvable from the following URL: http://www.isni.org/<identifier>.

comment.en: The International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI) is an identifier system for uniquely identifying the public identities of contributors to media content.
The Digital Author Identification system assigns a unique number to all authors in the Netherlands research system.

scopeNote.value: A GitLab user account is resolvable from the following URL: https://gitlab.com/<identifier>.

comment.en: The GitLab user account is a unique identifier assigned to GitLab users.

scopeNote.value: A ResearchGate profile identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/<identifier>.

comment.en: The ResearchGate profile identifier is a unique code for researchers registered in the ResearchGate platform.

scopeNote.value: A Google Scholar author identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=<identifier>.

comment.en: The Google Scholar author identifier is a unique identifier assigned to authors signed to Google Scholar.
OpenID is an open standard that describes how users can be authenticated in a decentralized manner, eliminating the need for centralized registration services.

scopeNote.value: A GEPRIS person identifier is resolvable from the following URL: http://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/person/<identifier>.

comment.en: The GEPRIS person identifier is a unique, numerical identifier assigned to researchers and investigators in the GEPRIS database.

scopeNote.value: A DBLP author identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://dblp.org/pid/<identifier>.

comment.en: The DBLP author identifier is a unique key assigned to each researcher registered on DBLP.

scopeNote.value: A VIAF identifier is resolvable from the following URL: http://viaf.org/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Virtual International Authority File (VIAF) is an international authority file created by amalagamating the national authority files of several national libraries and operated by the Online Computer Library Center (OCLC). It contains information about many topics including personal names.
The ResearcherID is an identifying system for scientific authors created and owned by Thomson Reuters.
The United States of America social security number is a nine-digit number issued to U.S. residents.
A personal identifier scheme that provides local personal identifiers that are unique in their local environment and understood by the person submitting the metadata.
The identifier scheme used to identify a person.

scopeNote.value: A rights identifier belongs to a particular scheme, such as SPDX, specified by an individual within the class datacite:RightsIdentifierScheme.

comment.en: An identifier that uniquely identifies a license.

scopeNote.value: Individual schemes are defines as members of this class.
A Crossref member identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://api.crossref.org/members/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Crossref member identifier is a unique numerical ID automatically assigned to each organization when they join Crossref to manage their account and content registration.

scopeNote.value: A ROR identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://ror.org/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Research Organization Registry (ROR) Community identifier is a unique code assigned to research organizations.

scopeNote.value: An ISNI is resolvable from the following URL: http://www.isni.org/<identifier>.

comment.en: The International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI) is an identifier system for uniquely identifying the public identities of contributors to media content.
An organization identifier scheme that provides local organization identifiers that are unique in their local environment and understood by the person submitting the metadata.
The identifier scheme used to identify an organization.
It describes reified literals, where the literal value they represent is speficied through the property litre:hasLiteralValue. Each individual of this class must always have a specified value.

scopeNote.value: An alternate resource identifier belongs to a particular scheme, such as ISBN, specified by an individual that is a member of the class datacite:ResourceIdentifierScheme.

comment.en: An identifier other than a DOI that is used as an alternative identifier to uniquely identify a resource that is the subject of the DataCite metadata record.

scopeNote.value: A funder identifier belongs to a particular scheme, such as FundRef, specified by an individual within the class datacite:FunderIdentifierScheme.

comment.en: An identifier that uniquely identities a funding agency.
A class representing a reified relation between two resources, allowing the assignment of a specific role or type to the connection.

scopeNote.value: Neither a class for metadata documents nor a property linking a resource to its metadata document are explicitly defined in this ontology. However, we recommend to use the class fabio:MetadataDocument (from http://purl.org/spar/fabio) and cito:citesAsMetadataDocument (from http://purl.org/spar/cito) for providing such descriptions. In addition, if needed, it is possible to use the dataproperty fabio:hasURL (not included in this ontology as well) for defining the actual URL of a certain metadata scheme.

comment.en: The Semantic Publishing and Referencing Ontologies, a.k.a. SPAR Ontologies, form a suite of orthogonal and complementary OWL 2 DL ontology modules for the creation of comprehensive machine-readable RDF metadata for every aspect of semantic publishing and referencing: document description, bibliographic resource identifiers, types of citations and related contexts, bibliographic references, document parts and status, agents' roles and contributions, bibliometric data and workflow processes.
The class that describe metadata schemes used for creating a metadata document referring to a certain resource.

scopeNote.value: This class uses a datacite:IdentiferScheme that is restricted to datacite:doi, an individual in the datacite:ResourceIdentifierScheme.

comment.en: An identifier that is used as the primary identifier to uniquely identifies the primary resource that is the subject of the DataCite metadata record.
The Directory of Open Access Repositories (OpenDOAR) is a service that lists open access repositories, and uses numerical internal identifiers to store their record.
An identifier that is used to uniquely identify a resource.

scopeNote.value: An agent identifier belongs to a particular identifier scheme, specified by an individual within the class datacite:AgentIdentifierScheme (or any of its subclasses).

comment.en: An identifier that uniquely identities an individual agent.

A Lattes Platform number is resolvable from the following URL: http://lattes.cnpq.br/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Lattes Platform number is an identifier for a Lattes Platform entry related to a person or group.

scopeNote.value: An ORCID is resolvable from the following URL: http://orcid.org/<identifier>.

comment.en: The Open Researcher and Contributor Identifier (ORCID) is a unique identifier for individuals to use as they engage in research, scholarship, and innovation activities.

scopeNote.value: A LinkedIn personal profile identifier is resolvable from the following URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/<identifier>.

comment.en: The LinkedIn personal profile identifier is an unique identifier assigned to a LinkedIn user.

scopeNote.value: A GitHub username is resolvable from the following URL: https://github.com/<identifier>.

comment.en: The GitHub username is a unique identifier assigned to GitHub users.

scopeNote.value: A Twitter handle is resolvable from the following URL: https://twitter.com/<identifier>.

comment.en: A Twitter handle is the unique identifier assigned to Twitter users.

scopeNote.value: This property uses as range an existing property via OWL2 punning, according to which it becomes possible to use an object property as the object of an OWL assertion. In such cases of OWL punning, the object properties are simultaneously considered both as normal object properties and also as proper named individuals of the class owl:Thing.
